title: E-Beam Inspection - ESD Damage Detection on Teron 640
subtitle: Post-Oxidation Quality Validation for 65nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Wei Zhang

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Teron 640 system to detect and classify ESD Damage defects during post-oxidation inspection at the 65nm technology node. The test is conducted at Milpitas Fab A to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for ESD Damage defects that are critical to yield at the 65nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Teron 640 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Teron 640
- Inspection Type: E-Beam Inspection
- Target Defect: ESD Damage
- Process Step: Post-Oxidation
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 65nm
- Fab Location: Milpitas Fab A

This test case applies to all Teron 640 systems deployed at Milpitas Fab A for post-oxidation monitoring in the 65nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Teron 640
Software Version: v8.2.999
Recipe: E-BEAM_INSPECTION_65nm_POST_OXIDATION
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Medium (108 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.25μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: 5-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Teron 640 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'E-Beam Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target ESD Damage defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 65nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 117 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 96% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.2% for E-Beam Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.95 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-01-14
Wafers Tested: 42
Total Defects Found: 2607
Defect Density: 829.83 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 1.3%
Capture Rate: 91.7%
Test Duration: 386 minutes
System Uptime: 97.0%

Result Classification: PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Teron 640 demonstrated excellent performance in detecting ESD Damage at the 65nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) Recipe portability between systems at this fab was confirmed.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS: No corrective actions required. Test passed all acceptance criteria.
